_note: Phase 8 load cases and member sizes for `suspkin loads` (see solver/suspkin/loads.py). Accelerations are in g at the car's CG; car-level numbers (mass, weight split, CG height, wheelbase) come from the FRONT hardpoints file and the lateral load transfer split from `suspkin car`. Every tyre is assumed to use the same share of its grip, so its forces are proportional to its own vertical load. Made-up FSAE-style numbers: change them to suit.
_safety_factor_note: Each member must carry at least this many times its worst load case before yielding, buckling or reaching its rod end rating. The g levels below are already peak values (a little above the 1.5 g design load), so 1.5 on top is a common choice for a hobby / FSAE-style design.

cases.name: cornering
cases._why: Peak steady cornering, a little above the 1.5 g design load. The inside front tyre lifts at about 1.9 g, so this stays below lift-off.

cases.name: braking
cases._why: Peak straight-line braking, all four tyres at the same friction use.

cases.name: braking_cornering
cases._why: Trail braking into a corner: about 1.56 g combined, on the friction circle.

cases.name: acceleration
cases._why: Traction-limited launch: only the driven (rear) axle pushes.

cases.name: bump
cases._why: Pothole / kerb strike: 3 times the static corner load, straight up.

_pneumatic_trail_note: A cornering tyre's sideways force acts a little behind the middle of its contact patch (its self-aligning torque). Without it the rear toe link would carry nothing in a corner, because the rear has no caster. 15-30 mm is typical for small racing tyres near peak grip.

material.name: AISI 4130 chromoly, normalised
material._note: Welding softens the tube next to the weld (heat-affected zone) to roughly 360 MPa unless it is heat treated after. Not modelled: the safety factor has to cover it.

_effective_length_note: K for buckling. 1.0 = pinned at both ends (rod ends / spherical bearings), with the length taken centre to centre of the joints, which is a little conservative.
_members_note: Tube sizes match the Fusion script's defaults (cad/fusion/SuspensionModel). On the rear corner 'tie_rod' is the toe link. Rod end and ball joint ratings are PLACEHOLDERS: replace them with the static radial load rating from the catalogue of the parts you would actually buy.
_tube_catalogue_note: Common inch chromoly tube sizes, [outside diameter, wall] in mm (1/2 to 1 in OD, 0.035 / 0.049 / 0.065 in wall). `suspkin loads` reports the lightest one that passes for each member group.
